cases.name: no-stack-questions-one-at-a-time
cases.prompt: I want a small internal tool that archives our team's Slack channels somewhere so we can still search old conversations after Slack's free-plan history limit kicks in. Before anyone writes a spec or code, help me pin down what I actually want. We'll continue this conversation turn by turn.
cases.trap: Without guidance a model fires a long questionnaire in one turn and asks the user to pick language, database, storage backend or hosting, which are ordinary expert decisions.
expectations: Asks a single consequential question in this turn (or a tightly coupled pair), not a numbered questionnaire

The question concerns a user-owned outcome, scope or trade-off, e.g. which channels or message types must be preserved, who must be able to search, whether private channels/DMs are in scope, or how long archives must be kept
Offers a recommended answer with a short reason and names at least one meaningful alternative
negative_expectations: Asks the user to choose a programming language, database, search engine, cloud storage provider or library
Produces a full spec, architecture or task breakdown before the intent is clarified
Asks five or more separate questions in the same turn

cases.name: answer-from-evidence-first
cases.prompt: We're adding automatic purging of old audit-log entries. Clarify my intent before we write it up. Relevant repo excerpt, docs/decisions/0007-audit-retention.md (status: accepted by product owner, 2026-03-02): 'Audit entries are retained for 400 days. Entries under legal hold are retained until the hold is lifted.' README: 'Audit logs are visible to org admins only.'
cases.trap: A model without the skill re-asks the retention period, legal-hold handling or visibility even though an accepted decision already answers them, fires a multi-question list, or asks about implementation choices such as scheduler, delete mechanism or backups.
expectations: Uses the 400-day retention and legal-hold rule from the accepted decision rather than asking the user for them

Asks one consequential question about something the excerpts leave open (e.g. whether purge must be recoverable, whether admins are notified or can see what was purged, whether existing over-age entries are purged immediately)
Gives a recommended answer for that question and names at least one meaningful alternative
negative_expectations: Asks the user how long audit entries should be kept
Asks whether entries under legal hold should be purged
Proposes a different retention period as if it were undecided
Asks five or more separate questions in the same turn
Asks about scheduler, delete mechanism, backups or other implementation choices
